raw_response:
I will mostly do what has worked for me here, then adjust a little for cost and water. I have 8 mu total, and with wheat-maize as my main system, I will keep most land in that rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. I will put 5 mu into winter wheat, then that same 5 mu will go into summer maize after harvest. The other 3 mu I will keep in cotton. I have only two people at home, so I will not make the management too complicated. I do have well irrigation, so I will use water at the key times instead of gambling on rain.

For wheat, I will use an improved seed because around here if the variety is old, the stand and yield are not steady. I will still put enough fertilizer because if wheat comes up weak in winter and spring, it is hard to pull it back later. I will use rotary tillage for convenience on my 5 mu, put more base fertilizer in, then topdress once when the seedlings start taking off in spring. I will water about 3 times if the year is normal: one after sowing or at wintering if dry, one at jointing, and one at filling if needed. I will spray about 2 times, mainly for weeds and then disease or aphids if they show up.

For summer maize, I will follow right after wheat harvest on the same 5 mu. I will use hybrid seed because that has been normal for years and gives better ears if fertilizer and water keep up. Maize eats fertilizer hard, so I will not go too light. I will do rotary tillage after wheat, or shallow incorporation with the machine, then sow quickly so I do not lose moisture. I will water about 2 times with the well, one around big flare stage and one around silking or grain filling depending on rain. I will spray about 2 times, one for weeds early and one for insects later if pressure comes.

For cotton, I will keep 3 mu because cotton still brings cash, but it takes more watching than grain. I will use improved seed, not the old saved kind. Cotton needs steady feeding, but I will not overspend because too much fertilizer can make it grow too much stalk. I will use a plough once before planting if the field is tight, then manage with 3 irrigations in a normal year. Cotton needs more pesticide than wheat and maize here, so I will expect about 4 sprays through the season for worms, aphids, and mites if they come. Yield for cotton I judge by seed cotton, and if the weather is decent, I will aim for a solid middle yield rather than chase a risky high one.
